I will keep my land use simple this year because I am 75, my farm is only 6 mu, and some people in my family work off-farm, so I cannot rely on too much labor. I will still put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation because that is the most familiar and steady system for me in Quzhou County, and I have well irrigation, so I can support both crops when water is needed. I will keep a smaller part in cotton, not a big area, because cotton needs more picking and more field watching, and at my age I do not want to make the work too heavy. For wheat, I will use improved seed and manage fertilizer and water steadily because wheat is my base grain crop and I want a safe yield. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because the return is usually better and the crop fits well after wheat. I will use no-tillage for maize after wheat harvest to save time and labor. For cotton, I will keep inputs moderate, with enough potassium and several pesticide sprays, because cotton needs more protection but I do not want to overinvest on such a small farm. Overall, I will aim for stable production, manageable labor, and low risk rather than chasing the highest possible yield.
